# `record where` for [filters](/commands/categories/filters.md)

<div class='command-title'>Keep the fields of a record for which a row condition or closure is true.</div>

## Command Type

`built-in`

## Signature

```> record where {flags} (condition)```

## Flags

 -  `--keys, -k`: Pass only the key, as `$it` in a row condition, as a closure's argument, and as `$in`.
 -  `--values, -v`: Pass only the value, as `$it` in a row condition, as a closure's argument, and as `$in`.

## Parameters

 -  `condition`: The row condition or closure that decides whether to keep each field.


## Input/output types:

| input     | output    |
| --------- | --------- |
| record    | record    |
| table     | table     |
| list&lt;any&gt; | list&lt;any&gt; |
## Examples

Keep the fields whose value is greater than one.
```nu
> {a: 1, b: 2, c: 3} | record where value > 1
╭───┬───╮
│ b │ 2 │
│ c │ 3 │
╰───┴───╯
```

Keep the fields whose key starts with `NU_`.
```nu
> {NU_LOG: debug, HOME: /home/me, NU_THEME: dark} | record where key starts-with NU_
╭──────────┬───────╮
│ NU_LOG   │ debug │
│ NU_THEME │ dark  │
╰──────────┴───────╯
```

Keep the fields whose value is greater than one, with a closure.
```nu
> {a: 1, b: 2, c: 3} | record where {|key, value| $value > 1}
╭───┬───╮
│ b │ 2 │
│ c │ 3 │
╰───┴───╯
```

Drop the fields with empty values.
```nu
> {name: app, desc: '', tags: []} | record where --values { is-not-empty }
╭──────┬─────╮
│ name │ app │
╰──────┴─────╯
```

Drop the empty fields of every row of a table.
```nu
> [{a: 1, b: ''} {a: '', b: 2}] | record where --values { is-not-empty }
╭───┬────┬────╮
│ # │ a  │ b  │
├───┼────┼────┤
│ 0 │  1 │ ❎ │
│ 1 │ ❎ │  2 │
╰───┴────┴────╯

```

## Notes
A row condition sees each field as a `{key, value}` record, the rows `where` would see after `transpose key value`. So `record where value > 1` filters on the value and `record where key starts-with NU_` on the key.
A closure instead receives each field's key and value as two arguments, like `items`, and `$in` is empty.
With `--keys` or `--values`, the condition receives only the key or only the value. A row condition gets it as `$it`, a closure as its argument, and both as `$in`, so a closure needs no parameters.
Put `--keys` and `--values` before the condition, because a row condition takes everything after it.
`record where` keeps the matching fields in their original order.
Given a list of records, each record is filtered on its own and the results are streamed.
